items.headline: NEA raises cremation and niche fees from January 2027 in first revision since 1997
items.summary: Government cremation fees for citizens and permanent residents will rise from S$100 to S$175 (and to S$350 for others) from 1 January 2027, with standard niche fees up from S$500 to S$600 and compulsory burial from S$315 to S$400, while inland ash-scattering falls from S$320 to S$200; ComCare and ComLink+ households get full waivers.

items.headline: Singapore's resident labour force participation rate dips to 67.8% in 2026
items.summary: The Manpower Ministry's advance release shows the resident labour force participation rate for those aged 15 and over slipped to 67.8% from 67.9% in 2025 amid an ageing population, even as overall unemployment stayed low; the number of residents outside the labour force rose to about 1.18 million.

items.headline: Singapore raises its 2026 growth forecast to around 6% after a 6.1% third quarter
items.summary: The Trade and Industry Ministry lifted its 2026 GDP forecast to about 6%, up from a 4.5-5.5% range, after third-quarter growth came in at 6.1% year-on-year, beating the 5.4% advance estimate; Enterprise Singapore raised its 2026 non-oil domestic export growth projection to 30-32%.

items.headline: Chief Justice Menon sets out a 'communitarian' rule of law at a Singapore conference
items.summary: At a Global Rule of Law Conference in Singapore marking the Judiciary's bicentennial, Chief Justice Sundaresh Menon and Home and Law Minister K. Shanmugam set out a rule of law that balances individual rights with society's needs; the gathering drew about 600 delegates from 26 jurisdictions, including current and former foreign chief justices.

items.headline: Supreme Court quashes Anand Mohan's remission, says victims must be heard before release
items.summary: The Supreme Court on 26 November struck down Bihar's 2023 rule change that freed former MP Anand Mohan, jailed for life over the 1994 murder of IAS officer G. Krishnaiah, and ordered him to surrender within a month; the bench held that victims have an Article 21 right to be heard before remission, though their objection is not a veto.

items.headline: India calls a special Parliament sitting from November 30 amid delimitation speculation
items.summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju asked the Lok Sabha to reconvene on 30 November and the Rajya Sabha on 2 December for what he called 'very significant business' as a continuation of the Monsoon Session, without confirming the agenda; the opposition INDIA bloc called a strategy meeting, expecting a push on the stalled Delimitation Bill.

items.headline: Tripura records about 80% turnout in urban local body polls amid opposition complaints
items.summary: Polling across 16 of Tripura's urban local bodies on 27 November drew roughly 80% turnout, with about 4.41 lakh of 5.62 lakh voters casting ballots by late afternoon; the BJP had already won 77 seats unopposed, the opposition alleged intimidation and counting is set for 2 December.

items.headline: India's July-September GDP data is due November 30, with growth seen around 7.6%
items.summary: Official second-quarter FY27 GDP lands on 30 November; a Mint poll of economists forecasts about 7.6% year-on-year growth, down from 7.8% the prior quarter but above the Reserve Bank's 7.2% projection, with SBI Research estimating 7.8% and ICRA 7.5%.

items.headline: Huntingdon train attacker Anthony Williams convicted of 14 attempted murders
items.summary: A jury at Cambridge Crown Court on 26 November found Anthony Williams, 33, guilty of attempting to murder 14 people — 10 on an LNER London-bound train that made an emergency stop at Huntingdon on 1 November 2025, plus three in Peterborough and one on a DLR train; he appeared by video-link from a secure hospital and will be sentenced on 4-5 February.

items.headline: MPs urge the NHS to set a bed-occupancy target and end 'corridor care' for children
items.summary: A Commons committee on 27 November urged the government to adopt a hospital bed-occupancy target and a plan to end corridor care for children, warning of a 'stark' gap between ministers' optimism and front-line NHS staff as the service heads into winter.

items.headline: UK tribunal rejects the government's bid to keep its Apple encryption order secret
items.summary: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal ruled that the government cannot keep secret its order demanding access to Apple users' encrypted data, allowing some future proceedings in the case to be held in public; the decision was made public on 19 November.

items.headline: UK government opens an investigation into Birmingham's supported housing sector
items.summary: Ministers launched an investigation into supported 'exempt' accommodation in Birmingham — which houses around 34,000 benefit claimants across about 12,200 properties — following a High Court ruling that found a provider was taking advantage of the benefits system.

items.headline: EU summit collapses without a budget deal or a EUR45bn Ukraine loan
items.summary: An extraordinary EU summit in Brussels broke up early on 27 November with no agreement on the 2028-2034 budget or on a new EUR45 billion loan for Ukraine; Council President Antonio Costa said leaders agreed on none of the budget's main elements, and the matter was pushed to a 17-18 December summit as Germany's Friedrich Merz pressed for deeper cuts.

items.headline: Two Italian defence technicians killed in a drone strike on a Kuwait air-defence site
items.summary: Antonio Saccoccio, 65, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, of Rheinmetall Italia were killed on 26 November while servicing an air-defence system at a Kuwaiti facility, with two other workers wounded; Italy's foreign minister said the drone was Iranian-made, while Iran's embassy in Rome denied any involvement.

items.headline: Colombian forces end a supermarket hostage siege in Cartagena
items.summary: Colombian special forces freed the remaining hostages to end a roughly day-long siege at a supermarket in Cartagena on 25 November; one captor was killed and two suspects captured, and the gunmen had demanded about 7 billion pesos after a failed armoured-vehicle robbery.

items.headline: Germany arrests two Iraqis over an alleged Iran-linked plot to bomb synagogues
items.summary: German federal prosecutors arrested two Iraqi men in Heidelberg and Cologne on 26 November over an alleged plot, tied to a pro-Iranian group, to attack synagogues; the raids involved more than 250 officers across 17 sites, and prosecutors say a search for a further suspect continues.

items.headline: Nvidia pauses server shipments to Southeast Asia amid a US export crackdown
items.summary: Nvidia asked manufacturing partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it checks whether regional partners comply with US export rules, after Washington closed a loophole that let Chinese firms rent computing power from data centres in those countries.

items.headline: Restricted Nvidia Blackwell AI racks surface at a Shanghai data centre
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Chinese loan filings show a restricted Nvidia GB300 rack pledged as collateral and a GB200 server at a Shanghai site tied to the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, which the US added to its Entity List on 23 November; Megaspeed and Nvidia deny any diversion.

items.headline: US export rule requiring licences for Chinese firms' remote chip access takes effect
items.summary: A US Commerce Department interim rule that took effect on 19 November requires licences to export advanced AI chips and servers to data centres anywhere that may supply computing power to companies in China or other restricted countries, tightening controls on remote access to Nvidia hardware.

items.headline: OpenAI raises about $11 billion more at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised roughly $11 billion so far in a funding round valuing it at about $1.25 trillion; the round could total around $20 billion, short of the roughly $30 billion the company had sought.

items.headline: Wall Street rallies on Black Friday as the Nasdaq caps its best week in months
items.summary: In a holiday-shortened session on 27 November the Dow rose about 1.2% to 50,775, the S&P 500 1.6% to 7,297 and the Nasdaq 2.3% to 24,130; all three gained more than 5% on the week — the S&P's best since April 2025 — as AI and chip stocks rebounded.

items.headline: US Thanksgiving online sales hit a record $7.1 billion
items.summary: Americans spent about $7.1 billion online on Thanksgiving Day, up 10.4% from a year earlier and above Adobe's $6.9 billion forecast, with phones accounting for roughly 63% of spending; Adobe projects a record $12.9 billion Black Friday and $15.1 billion Cyber Monday.

items.headline: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO, powering a chip-stock rebound
items.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously on 23 November to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive about 11 days after he resigned amid a scandal, citing input from senior US government levels; the stock jumped more than 30% and helped drive the week's AI-led market rebound.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli heads Friday practice as the Qatar Grand Prix weekend begins
items.summary: Newly crowned 2026 champion Kimi Antonelli was fastest for Mercedes in Friday practice at Lusail, heading team-mate George Russell with Lando Norris close behind; qualifying follows on Saturday and the race on Sunday, the penultimate round of the season.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli reaches Qatar as F1's youngest champion with Mercedes eyeing the constructors' title
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli clinched the 2026 drivers' title at the Mexico City Grand Prix to become F1's youngest champion at 20 and the first Italian champion since 1953; with the drivers' fight settled, Mercedes lead the constructors' standings and can edge closer to that title over the final two rounds.

items.headline: 🏏 India reduce New Zealand to 246 for 5 on day one of the second Test in Christchurch
items.summary: After winning the toss and bowling first at Hagley Oval, India had New Zealand at 246 for 5 at stumps on day one of the second Test, with Tom Latham making 59, Tom Blundell 53 not out and Glenn Phillips 36 not out after India struck early.

items.headline: 🎾 Great Britain face Spain and Italy meet Czechia in the Davis Cup semi-finals
items.summary: Great Britain, in their first Davis Cup semi-final since 2019 after beating Germany 2-1, face Spain — 2-0 winners over Austria — in Bologna, while holders Italy take on Czechia in the other semi-final; the final is on Sunday.

items.headline: Voyager 1 becomes the first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
items.summary: NASA says Voyager 1 passed one light-day from Earth — about 16.1 billion miles — on 18 November, the first human-made object to do so after nearly 50 years in space; a radio signal from the probe now takes a full 24 hours to reach home.

items.headline: Europe's BepiColombo settles into orbit around Mercury despite a thruster glitch
items.summary: The ESA-JAXA BepiColombo mission entered orbit around Mercury on 21 November — only the second mission ever to do so — after a planned braking burn was cut short by a software glitch, leaving it in a 75-hour orbit rather than the intended 58-hour one; ESA says the spacecraft is safe and stable, with its two orbiters due to separate on 9 December.

items.headline: Tau-targeting Alzheimer's therapy reports slower decline in a phase 2 trial
items.summary: Two-year results presented at a major Alzheimer's conference showed that diranersen, an antisense therapy targeting the tau protein, slowed clinical decline by about 38% at its highest dose versus placebo, though it missed its main statistical goal; the developer plans a larger phase 3 study.

items.headline: A dark-matter telescope turns up an unexpected find: Euclid's first comet
items.summary: While scanning the sky for clues to dark matter, ESA's Euclid space telescope captured a previously unknown comet, now designated C/2026 S1 (Euclid), spotted by a PhD student working with the Euclid Consortium; the icy visitor could help pick a target for the planned Comet Interceptor mission.

fun_fact.headline: Gallium is a metal that melts in your hand
fun_fact.body: Gallium is a soft, silvery metal that melts at about 29.8°C — just below body temperature — so a solid lump will turn to liquid in the warmth of your hand and set solid again once you put it down. Despite melting so easily it does not boil until around 2,200°C, one of the widest liquid ranges of any element, and unlike mercury it is barely toxic to handle.
fun_fact.source: Wikipedia; Royal Society of Chemistry; Live Science

puzzle.title: Hands Together
puzzle.body:
A clock reads exactly 3:00, so the hour hand is on the 3 and the minute hand on the 12. Some time in the next hour the two hands will point in exactly the same direction and overlap.

At what time, to the nearest second, does this happen?
puzzle.approach: Work out how many degrees each hand sweeps per minute, then find when they meet.
puzzle.answer:
The minute hand sweeps 360° in 60 minutes = 6° per minute. The hour hand sweeps 360° in 12 hours = 0.5° per minute.

At 3:00 the hour hand sits at 90° (3 × 30°) and the minute hand at 0°. After t minutes the minute hand is at 6t° and the hour hand at (90 + 0.5t)°. They meet when 6t = 90 + 0.5t, so 5.5t = 90 and t = 90 ÷ 5.5 = 16 and 4/11 minutes.

That is 16 minutes and about 21.8 seconds, so the hands overlap at roughly 3:16:22.

word_puzzle.title: Says It All
word_puzzle.body:
Rearrange the letters of each clue into a new word or phrase that aptly describes it. The target letter-pattern is shown in brackets.

1. DORMITORY → (5, 4)
2. THE MORSE CODE → (4, 4, 4)
3. THE CLASSROOM → a one-word profession (12)
word_puzzle.approach: Each capitalised clue is an 'apt anagram' — rearrange all its letters into a new word or phrase that describes the clue itself.
word_puzzle.answer:
1. DORMITORY → DIRTY ROOM
2. THE MORSE CODE → HERE COME DOTS
3. THE CLASSROOM → SCHOOLMASTER

Each answer uses exactly the same letters as its clue.

notes: Environment: WebFetch to news domains blocked and US-only WebSearch rarely surfaced deep article URLs for several allowed outlets (BBC, Sky, Reuters, The Hindu, NDTV, CNA, ST). Every item was cross-verified against 2+ independent outlets. Where an allowed-outlet deep URL did not surface, items cite a reputable outlet or primary source whose URL was retrievable: Singapore used primary government releases (NEA, MOM, MHA) plus a Reuters wire; India cited ThePrint/India TV/Deccan Chronicle/KNN India (allowed Indian outlets' deep URLs did not surface, nor did the international fallback desks cover these domestic stories); UK used ITV, Bloomberg (fallback tier), Inside Housing and UK Parliament as BBC/Sky deep URLs did not surface; Global cited Euronews and The New Arab for the EU-budget and Germany items where allowed-outlet URLs did not surface (Al Jazeera used for two). Tech skewed to the US-China chip-controls story this week; two tech items are from earlier in November. Business carries 3 items (the prior three days ran 11 markets stories; fresh oil/gold moves lacked a retrievable allowed-source URL). Sports live Saturday results (F1 qualifying, cricket day 2, Davis Cup semi-finals) had not occurred/indexed at publish time, so items report the latest confirmed state. No spectrum/bias blocks this edition (could not confirm three distinct real-outlet framings).
